concepts.def: A community of organisms together with their physical environment.
Shows the flow of energy from producers to consumers.
Makes its own food by photosynthesis; the start of a food chain.
Breaks down dead matter, recycling nutrients.
Interlinked food chains showing feeding relationships.
Recycles carbon via respiration, photosynthesis, combustion and decay.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecological Relationships — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecological Relationships brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecological Relationships.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cell”?
options: The smallest unit of life; carries out the functions needed to live.
Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
Cells adapted for a specific role, e.g. red blood cell, sperm, root hair.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stem cell”?
options: Parts inside a cell with specific jobs: nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, chloroplasts.
A cell with a nucleus enclosed in a membrane; e.g. animal, plant, fungus cells.
Undifferentiated cell that can divide to form many cell types.
A smaller cell with no nucleus; DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm; e.g. bacteria.
